title: The Decline of Western Men: From Cult of Strength to Church of Weakness
summary: Final part of NH's Educated Barbarian cycle on Nietzsche and religion. He argues religion once restrained and civilized strong men and gave meaning to suffering, but once strength ran out it became a 'church of weakness' that preserves sufferers, breeds resentment of greatness and produced the mediocre modern European man.
claims: Nietzsche ties the decline of European men directly to the decline of religion
Nietzsche was not anti-religion; he saw it as a man-made system for organizing men, a civilizational tool rather than something divine
Religion is mankind's refinery: it shaped behavior culturally, restraining might-makes-right barbarism so societies could exist
Asceticism and puritanism were necessary evils; the problem is that religion went too far
What Nietzsche detested most was the deception of moral preachers who used religion to control the masses rather than in earnest
The Brahmin caste is Nietzsche's example of a spiritual class controlling political power while keeping itself apart from its corrupting labor
Religion gave class mobility: the Bible forced peasants to learn to read and opened the path to intellectuality, self-control and solitude
Religion turned barbarian knights who raped and pillaged into refined, courteous, chivalrous gentlemen
Religion made the lower classes content by ennobling obedience; removing it exposed hierarchies and gave rise to class warfare
Christianity gave meaning to suffering; without it suffering is pain without meaning, which is why modern people complain constantly
Religion goes astray when it becomes an end instead of a means; the machine built to restrain strength keeps pushing toward weakness once strength is gone, creating a church of weakness
Inequality of outcomes is now treated as injustice, so greatness becomes rarer while a surplus of failure is preserved
'Eat the rich' is resentment of those who did better; France in particular despises success and assumes winners cheated
Religion for suffering has become religion for sufferers: it shelters those who suffer without giving them a way out and opens the path to resentment of successful people
Modern religions, atheism and scientism included, demonize the will to power and present the will to survival as true morality
The slave revolt works by exploiting strong men's sympathy for the weak, convincing them their own superior position is unjust
Modern culture casts suspicion on beauty, so working on your body is seen as vain
Governments strip citizens of independence so they become dependent on systems they believe they cannot live without
NH believes modern humans are devolving rather than progressing
Nietzsche detested equality because in practice it means equality in mediocrity
